target.title: fix(matrix): honor abortSignal during startup whoami retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`backfillMatrixAuthDeviceIdAfterStartup` in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/config.ts` checks `params.abortSignal` before and after the startup `whoami` call, and the production caller (`monitor/index.ts`) passes a real signal. But the `whoami` request itself retries via `retryMatrixAuthRequest` with an unabortable backoff (250ms→1.5s). An abort landing inside that backoff was only noticed after the sleep elapsed and a second `whoami` request had been issued.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryMatrixAuthRequest` now accepts an optional `signal` and sleeps via `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` (same abort-aware helper as the merged #109604/#108561/#108408 sibling fixes). The backfill passes its `params.abortSignal` through `fetchMatrixWhoamiIdentity`. When the abort fires mid-backoff, the sleep's rejection propagates through `retryAsync`; a new `try/catch` in the backfill normalizes it to `undefined`, matching the contract of the existing post-`whoami` aborted checks. Non-abort failures still rethrow, and call sites that pass no signal (`resolveMatrixAuth`, password login) see zero behavior change — `sleepWithAbort(ms, undefined)` degenerates to the plain timer.

## Changes

- Thread an optional `signal` through `retryMatrixAuthRequest` and `fetchMatrixWhoamiIdentity`; backoff sleeps use `sleepWithAbort`.
- Pass `params.abortSignal` at the backfill call site; normalize abort rejection to `undefined` (no deviceId) while real network failures still propagate.
- Regression test: first `whoami` fails with a retryable `ECONNRESET`, abort fires inside the first 250ms backoff; asserts prompt `undefined`, exactly one request, and no deviceId persistence.

## User Impact

Stopping a Matrix account during startup no longer waits out the `whoami` retry backoff or issues a doomed second request; shutdown is prompt and no half-backfilled deviceId is persisted.

## Evidence

Exact head: `61bf06d32fffa32b079f9d641ef3203ec4de6c21`.

**Outside-runner behavior proof** — the production `backfillMatrixAuthDeviceIdAfterStartup` is driven directly (no test runner, no mocks) via `node --import tsx` against a real `node:http` loopback homeserver. The homeserver destroys the socket so `whoami` fails with a real transport `TypeError: fetch failed` (matches production `MATRIX_AUTH_REQUEST_RETRY_RE`); state dir is a real temp dir read back from disk afterward. Abort fires at the 200ms mark, inside the first backoff. A no-abort control scenario in the same run proves non-abort errors still rethrow after the full 3-attempt backoff.

After fix — abort during backoff returns `undefined` at the 200ms mark, exactly one `whoami` request, nothing persisted:

```text
$ env -C .worktrees/matrix-backfill-abort TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=/tmp/tsconfig.matrix-abort-proof.json node --import tsx /tmp/matrix-abort-proof.mts; echo "EXIT=$?"
[proof] config.ts sha256=7d330c7dddaaf66a
[proof] config.ts wires abort into backoff sleep: true
[proof] loopback homeserver: http://127.0.0.1:46085
[homeserver] whoami request #1 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: aborting startup now (200ms mark)
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: outcome=returned-undefined
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: elapsedMs=200.4
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: whoamiRequestCount=1
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: stateDirReadback files=0 deviceIdPersisted=false (state dir untouched)
[homeserver] whoami request #2 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[homeserver] whoami request #3 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[homeserver] whoami request #4 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: outcome=threw error="TypeError: fetch failed"
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: elapsedMs=794.8
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: whoamiRequestCount=3
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: stateDirReadback files=0 deviceIdPersisted=false (state dir untouched)
[proof] unhandledRejections=0
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 resolves undefined after abort
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 issued exactly 1 whoami request (got 1)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 shutdown prompt: elapsed 200.4ms < 2000ms
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 persisted nothing (no deviceId, no state files)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control rethrows non-abort retry exhaustion
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control made 3 attempts (got 3)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control ran the real backoff schedule (794.8ms)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control error is the transport failure
[proof] expect PASS: no unhandled promise rejections
[proof] RESULT: PASS
EXIT=0
```

Before fix (same script against `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/config.ts` from `upstream/main`, restored immediately after): the abort at 200ms is ignored, `whoami` requests #2 and #3 still go out, and the backfill throws at 846.6ms instead of returning promptly.

```text
[proof] config.ts sha256=61df451dc93086ce
[proof] config.ts wires abort into backoff sleep: false
[homeserver] whoami request #1 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: aborting startup now (200ms mark)
[homeserver] whoami request #2 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[homeserver] whoami request #3 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: outcome=threw error="TypeError: fetch failed"
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: elapsedMs=846.6
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: whoamiRequestCount=3
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: stateDirReadback files=0 deviceIdPersisted=false (state dir untouched)
[proof] expect FAIL: scenario1 resolves undefined after abort
[proof] expect FAIL: scenario1 issued exactly 1 whoami request (got 3)
[proof] RESULT: FAIL (2 unmet expectations)
EXIT=1
```

Regression tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  23 passed (23)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/index.test.ts
Tests  42 passed (42)
```

`oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions project reports no errors in matrix files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- The other `retryMatrixAuthRequest` call sites (`resolveMatrixAuth` startup whoami, password login) keep their current no-signal behavior; this PR only threads the signal where a real one already exists.
- No change to retry counts, delay bounds, or which errors are retryable.
